And then, everywhere else on the page, the same tiers wore different icons, or the same icon as each other, as if the top had never happened. His correction is not "make better icons" — the icons are already good. It is "use these ones again": the top's four are canonical, and canonical means everywhere — the chart header, the level rectangles, the nine chooser blocks, the calculator controls, the detail-view header. Same glyph, same color, every appearance. The sentence he repeated is the law itself, and it is worth quoting whole because it is the whole rule: "if that's what you're going to use then that's what you use. Everywhere." A good icon used once is a decoration. A good icon used everywhere is an identity — and identity is what lets the eye know which tier it is looking at without reading a word. That is the same law as round 14's colors, in a different object: the thing IS its mark, and the mark does not change from room to room.
